question: Difference between Hoya 58CIR or Hoya HMC ? Trying to decide between the regular Hoya Circular Polaraizing Filter or the HMC. Does the more expensive HMC give that much better results to justify the price?
gold_answer: Yes it does.  I would never consider using a non-multi-coated filter on a digital camera.  The reason is simple.  The sensor has a flat glass protecting it (called a low-pass filter - LPF).  Some light will bounce off the LPF and head out the lens.  Since lens elements are multi-coated and curved, very little light will reflect back to the sensor.  But since the front filter IS flat, you can get a lot of light bouncing back.  If you use a non-coated, or single-coated filter, you get a lot of light reflected back into the sensor.  This shows up as a loss of contrast (veiling flair) or as ghosts and hot spots.  Multi-coated filters are designed to reduce this effect, but cannot eliminate it.  This is a real problem when you shoot into a light source.When shooing into a light, ANY filter will degrade the image.  Multi-coated filters are much better, though.

question: can I refill the spools?
gold_answer: Okay. My earlier response to a similar question was yes and now i have more experience and knowledge to respond more thoroughly. a) yes, one can replace the line in these spools with thicker line. I have done so two times now using 0.08 in line i had leftover form my old dual line trimmer. I have the Greenworks 21242 G-MAX 40V model which is a single line design. These spools are only for single line machines.  They accommodate only one single line. B) When you load them with thicker line, there must-needs be less line length on the spool.  Thicker line works better for thicker stemmed plants and so will break less often in that case. However,...since my Greenworks 21242 G-MAX 40V trimmer has a "no bump" automatic line feed, the line is advanced 1/4 in every time you stop and start the motor.  If the weeds don't break the line, the cutter-knife thing will be cutting off that 1/4 in every time you stop. This means if you are only cutting grass and other less resistant weeds, the .065 in line is probably a better bet since there will be more line to use up per spool as you go about your standard trimming operations.  IF you have heavier weeds as i do, the .08 in line is a better bet since it is less likely to break for these tasks and if you are willing to continue trimming without stopping until the line has been shredded by the weeds.  i.e., more weeds per spool under such conditions.
